root_causes.cause: Origin server rejects requests from the newly deployed asset hostname, resulting in 403 Forbidden errors that propagate as 502 Bad Gateway responses for thumbnail requests.
evidence: ERROR log: "image transformer: origin fetch forbidden"
ERROR log: "new asset hostname deployed; origin status 403"
service_info indicates a recent deployment (synthetic-2026.11) coinciding with the appearance of the errors
checks: Inspect the origin server's access control list (ACL) or firewall rules for entries related to the new asset hostname.
Verify that the DNS entry for the new hostname resolves correctly to the origin.
Attempt a direct curl/wget request to the origin using the new hostname to reproduce the 403 response.
Review deployment configuration for any missing authentication tokens or headers required by the origin.
root_causes.fix: Update the origin server configuration (ACL, firewall, or authentication settings) to allow requests from the newly deployed asset hostname, and redeploy the media-gateway with the corrected settings.

off.explanation: All error logs point to a forbidden response from the origin when the media-gateway tries to fetch thumbnail assets after the recent deployment. A 403 from the origin typically causes the upstream service to return a 502 to the client. No other errors are present, making the origin access restriction the most plausible root cause. The suggested checks will confirm whether the hostname is blocked or misconfigured, and the fix addresses that specific issue.
off.memory_influence: No historical memories were available for this incident, so the diagnosis relies solely on the current logs and service information.

root_causes.cause: Incorrect Cloudflare R2 public bucket configuration combined with a new asset hostname deployment caused origin fetches to be forbidden (403), resulting in thumbnail 502 errors.
evidence: new asset hostname deployed; origin status 403 (log)
Catalogue thumbnails disappeared in the media-gateway service due to incorrect Cloudflare R2 public bucket configuration. (memory 7691ef8b-386a-481b-a904-9d2f58cc1e43)
New asset hostname deployment caused origin fetch to be forbidden (403 status). (memory a4521ec0-9d6f-4c6c-9356-a7f3acb0f964)

Incident INC-9021B79E occurred where catalogue thumbnails were unavailable in the media-gateway service due to an incorrect Cloudflare R2 public bucket configuration. (memory 5bfa3172-e7fb-43ad-a158-bdf6868f53f5)
checks: Verify that the Cloudflare R2 bucket is marked as public and that the public endpoint is enabled.
Confirm the asset hostname configured in media-gateway matches the bucket's allowed origins.
Perform a direct curl/wget request to a thumbnail URL using the new hostname to see if a 403 is returned.
Inspect Cloudflare R2 bucket CORS and IAM policies for restrictions on the new hostname.
root_causes.fix: Enable the R2 bucket's public endpoint (or adjust its access policy) and update the media-gateway asset origin configuration to reference the correct, publicly accessible hostname, then redeploy the service.

on.explanation: The logs show 502 errors for thumbnail requests and explicit messages that the origin fetch was forbidden (403) after a new asset hostname was deployed. Historical memories repeatedly attribute similar thumbnail outages to an incorrect Cloudflare R2 public bucket configuration and to the same hostname deployment causing forbidden fetches. No conflicting evidence was found; the current incident aligns with those past observations, indicating the root cause is a misconfigured public bucket combined with an unupdated hostname reference.
on.memory_influence: Memories 7691ef8b-386a-481b-a904-9d2f58cc1e43, a4521ec0-9d6f-4c6c-9356-a7f3acb0f964, and 5bfa3172-e7fb-43ad-a158-bdf6868f53f5 directly described the same failure mode (incorrect R2 public bucket settings and hostname deployment leading to 403 errors). These memories reinforced the diagnosis and guided the suggested checks and fix.
